newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Diesel prices at the pump poised to rise.
newsitem.headline: Diesel prices at the pump poised to rise.

text.p: Asia's drivers face higher diesel prices at the pump in coming months because of spiralling international market prices.
But refiners said they expect the pump price for gasoline to be steadier because demand from the west is slowing as its main driving season comes to an end.

High international diesel prices for most of 1996 are leading to the firmer pump price. International prices soared to a five-year record high of $29.70 per barrel last week, from a low of $23.00 per barrel on Singapore's international market in January. But even the 1996 low was one of the highest levels since 1993.
And for many Asian countries that has already translated into some of the highest diesel prices for motorists in years.
Diesel on London and New York's international markets are also trading at their highest levels since the 1990/1991 Gulf War.

Traders said the rise on Singapore's market is not due to an increased demand from China or India, Asia's biggest diesel consumers, but the effect of distillate stocks in the U.S. falling some 19 million barrels below 1995 levels as the peak demand fourth quarter begins.
"The demand and supply balance in Asia does not warrant such high prices. The market is dragged up by western fundamentals," a refiner in Singapore said.
Nevertheless, diesel prices at the pumps could rise further in the fourth quarter if international prices continue to spiral upwards.

Some Singapore refiners raised wholesale prices for the regional benchmark 0.5-percent sulphur diesel this week to around 70 cents per gallon. These compared with wholesale prices late last year in the low 50 cents per gallon.

Shell Singapore, the island's largest petroleum retailer, last raised its pump prices on March 7 by three Singapore cents to 50.1 cents per litre. At that time, the wholesale price was 65 cents per gallon.
Diesel prices at the pump in the Philippines, which are pegged on Singapore wholesale prices, breached seven pesos for the first time since 1992 to 7.07 peso per litre.

Prices in India are controlled by the state and are heavily subsidised by petrol consumers. Often a subject of political controversy, the Indian government was forced in July to halve a 30-percent price hike it had planned for diesel.
Thai diesel price are at their peak at 8.78 baht per litre compared with 7.40 baht a year ago, an official at state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand said.
Sri Lanka raised diesel prices late last month for the first time in two years to a record high of 13.20 rupees per litre from 12.40 rupees.
Diesel costs for motorists in Vietnam rose to 3,000 dong per litre to their highest levels in recent years, compared with 2,700 dong a year ago.
Analysts say there are other pressures on prices, like regulations for more environmentally friendly fuels.
Governments are increasingly demanding lower sulphur in fuel -- a cost that manufacturers have to pass on.
Thailand, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan all have legislation in place to bring sulphur content down to 0.1 or 0.05 percent by end-1999 or sooner.
Singapore's decision to lower sulphur content to 0.3 percent, which took effect in July, added about 0.5-1.0 cent per litre to manufacturing costs, refiners say.
